## Paragraph 25

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Paragraph 25] King’s Bench

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Paragraph 25] N/A

## SECTION C

## SPECIAL PROVISIONS

## 5.1 The following special provisions apply to the applications indicated.

## Applications under section 14 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 14 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] 6.1 This paragraph applies to an application under section 14 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878 for an order to rectify an omission or mis-statement in relation to the registration, or renewal of the registration, of a bill of sale—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 14 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (1) by inserting in the register the true name, residence or occupation of a person; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 14 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (2) by extending the time for registration of the bill of sale or an affidavit of its renewal.

## 6.2 The application must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.2 The application must be made—] (1) by claim form under Part 8; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.2 The application must be made—] (2) by witness statement.

## 6.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (1) Part 23 applies to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (2) the witness statement constitutes the application notice under that Part;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (3) the witness statement does not need to be served on any other person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (4) the application will normally be dealt with without a hearing.

## 6.4 The application must set out—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.4 The application must set out—] (1) the particulars of the bill of sale and of the omission or mis-statement; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.4 The application must set out—] (2) the grounds on which the application is made.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 6.4 The application must set out—] 6.5 The application must be made to a Master of the King’s Bench Division and accompanied by payment of the prescribed fee.

## Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] 7.1 This paragraph applies where an application is made under section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878 for an order that a memorandum of satisfaction be written on a registered copy of a bill of sale.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] 7.2 If the person entitled to the benefit of the bill of sale has not consented to the satisfaction, the claim form—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (1) must be served on that person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (2) must be supported by evidence that the debt (if any) for which the bill of sale was made has been satisfied or discharged.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] 7.3 If the person entitled to the benefit of the bill of sale has consented to the satisfaction, the application may be made by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (1) claim form under Part 8; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under Section 15 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] (2) witness statement.

## 7.4 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by Part 8 claim form, the claim form—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.4 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by Part 8 claim form, the claim form—] (1) must contain details of the consent;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.4 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by Part 8 claim form, the claim form—] (2) must be supported by a witness statement by a person who witnessed the consent verifying the signature on it; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.4 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by Part 8 claim form, the claim form—] (3) must not be served on any person other than the person entitled to the benefit of the bill of sale.

## 7.5 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by witness statement—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.5 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by witness statement—] (1) Part 23 will apply to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.5 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by witness statement—] (2) the witness statement will constitute the application notice under that Part;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.5 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by witness statement—] (3) the witness statement does not need to be served on any other person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 7.5 Where paragraph 11.3 applies and the application is made by witness statement—] (4) the application will normally be dealt with without a hearing.

## Applications under section 16 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 16 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878] 8.1 This paragraph applies to an application under section 16 of the Bills of Sale Act 1878 for a search of the bills of sale register and for a certificate of the results of the search.

## 8.2 The application must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 8.2 The application must be made—] (1) by claim form under Part 8; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 8.2 The application must be made—] (2) by written request.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 8.2 The application must be made—] 8.3 The application must give sufficient information to enable the relevant bill of sale to be identified.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 8.2 The application must be made—] 8.4 The application must be made to a Master of the King’s Bench Division and accompanied by payment of the prescribed fee.

## Application under the Public Trustee Act 1906

## 9.1 An application under the Public Trustee Act 1906 must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 9.1 An application under the Public Trustee Act 1906 must be made—] (1) where no proceedings have been issued, by a Part 8 claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 9.1 An application under the Public Trustee Act 1906 must be made—] (2) in existing proceedings, by a Part 23 application.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 9.1 An application under the Public Trustee Act 1906 must be made—] 9.2 Without prejudice to sections 10(2) and 13(7) of the Public Trustee Act 1906, the jurisdiction of the High Court under the Act is exercised by a single judge of the Chancery Division sitting in private.

## Applications under section 7 of the Deeds of Arrangement Act 1914

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 7 of the Deeds of Arrangement Act 1914] 10.1 This paragraph applies to an application under section 7 of the Deeds of Arrangement Act 1914 for an order to rectify an omission or mis-statement in relation to the registration of a deed of arrangement—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 7 of the Deeds of Arrangement Act 1914] (1) by inserting in the register the true name, residence or description of a person; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 7 of the Deeds of Arrangement Act 1914] (2) by extending the time for registration.

## 10.2 The application must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.2 The application must be made—] (1) by claim form under Part 8; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.2 The application must be made—] (2) by witness statement.

## 10.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (1) Part 23 applies to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (2) the witness statement constitutes the application notice under that Part;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (3) the witness statement does not need to be served on any other person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.3 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (4) the application will normally be dealt with without a hearing.

## 10.4 The application must set out—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.4 The application must set out—] (1) the particulars of the deed of arrangement and of the omission or mis-statement; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.4 The application must set out—] (2) the grounds on which the application is made.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 10.4 The application must set out—] 10.5 The application must be made to a Master of the King’s Bench Division and accompanied by payment of the prescribed fee.

## Application under section 2(3) of the Public Order Act 1936

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Application under section 2(3) of the Public Order Act 1936] 11.1 The Attorney General may determine the persons who should be made defendants to an application under section 2(3) of the Public Order Act 1936.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Application under section 2(3) of the Public Order Act 1936] 11.2 If the court directs an inquiry under section 2(3), it may appoint the Official Solicitor to represent any interests it considers are not sufficiently represented and ought to be represented.

## Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949] 12.1 Paragraphs 15.3 to 15.14 apply, with appropriate modifications, to proceedings in which jurisdiction has been conferred on the High Court by section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949, except to the extent that—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949] (1) an Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949] (2) a rule;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949] (3) a practice direction,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Proceedings under section 1 of the Railway and Canal Commission (Abolition) Act 1949] provides otherwise.

## Application under the Mines (Working Facilities and Support) Act 1966

## 13.1 In this paragraph—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.1 In this paragraph—] (1) ‘the Act’ means the Mines (Working Facilities and Support) Act 1966;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.1 In this paragraph—] (2) ‘the applicant’ means the person who has applied for the grant of a right under the Act.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.1 In this paragraph—] 13.2 This paragraph applies where the Secretary of State refers an application to the High Court under any provision of the Act.

## 13.3 The Secretary of State must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.3 The Secretary of State must—] (1) file a reference signed by him or a person authorised to sign on his behalf in the Chancery Division of the High Court;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.3 The Secretary of State must—] (2) file, along with the reference, any documents and plans deposited with him by the applicant in support of his application; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.3 The Secretary of State must—] (3) within 3 days of filing the reference, give notice to the applicant that the reference has been filed.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.3 The Secretary of State must—] 13.4 Within 10 days of receiving the notice referred to in paragraph 15.3(3), the applicant must issue a claim form.

## 13.5 The claim form—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.5 The claim form—] (1) must identify the application under the Act and the remedy sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.5 The claim form—] (2) need not be served on any other party.

## 13.6 Within 7 days of the claim form being issued, the applicant must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.6 Within 7 days of the claim form being issued, the applicant must—] (1) apply for the claim to be listed for a hearing before a Master; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.6 Within 7 days of the claim form being issued, the applicant must—] (2) give notice of the hearing date to the Secretary of State.

## 13.7 The applicant must, not less than 2 days before the date fixed for a hearing, file at court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.7 The applicant must, not less than 2 days before the date fixed for a hearing, file at court—] (1) a witness statement in support of the claim, giving details of all persons known to the applicant to be interested in, or affected by, the application; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.7 The applicant must, not less than 2 days before the date fixed for a hearing, file at court—] (2) a draft of any proposed advertisement or notice of the application.

## 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (1) fix a date by which any notice of objection under paragraph 15.9 must be filed;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (2) fix a date for a further hearing of the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (3) give directions about—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (a) any advertisement that is to be inserted or notice of the application and hearing date that is to be given; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (b) what persons are to be served with a copy of the application or any other document in the proceedings.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] 13.9 Any person who wishes to oppose the application must, within the time fixed by the court under paragraph 15.8, serve notice of objection on the applicant, stating—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (a) his name and address;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (b) the name and address of his solicitor, if any;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (c) the grounds of his objection;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (d) any alternative method for effecting the objects of the application that he alleges may be used; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (e) the facts on which he relies.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] 13.10 Any document that is required to be served on the person who has given notice of objection (‘the objector’) may be served by posting it to the following address—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (1) where the notice of objection gives the name and address of a solicitor, to the solicitor;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (2) in any other case, to the objector at the address stated in the notice of objection.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] 13.11 The objector may appear, or be represented at any further hearing, and may take such part in the proceedings as the court allows.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] 13.12 The applicant must, not less than two days before the date set for the further hearing, file at court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (1) any notices of objection served on him;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (2) a list of objectors, together with—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (a) their names and addresses;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (b) the names and addresses of their solicitors, if any; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.8 At the hearing, the Master will—] (c) a summary of their respective grounds of objection.

## 13.13 If the objector does not appear, or is not represented, at the further hearing—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.13 If the objector does not appear, or is not represented, at the further hearing—] (1) his notice of objection will have no effect; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.13 If the objector does not appear, or is not represented, at the further hearing—] (2) he will not be entitled to take any further part in the proceedings unless the court orders otherwise.

## 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (1) give directions about the future conduct of the claim, including—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (a) any further information the applicant is required to give in relation to any of the grounds or facts relied on in support of the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (b) any further information the objector is required to give in relation to any of the grounds or facts relied on in opposition to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (c) whether the applicant may serve a reply to any notice of objection;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (d) whether any particular fact should be proved by a witness statement;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (e) whether any statements of case or points of claim or defence are to be served; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 13.14 At the further hearing, the court will—] (2) adjourn the claim for hearing before a judge.

## Applications under article 10 of the Mortgaging of Aircraft Order 1972

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under article 10 of the Mortgaging of Aircraft Order 1972] 14.1 This paragraph applies to an application under article 10 of the Mortgaging of Aircraft Order 1972 for an order to amend the Register of Aircraft Mortgages.

## 14.2 The application must be made by claim form under Part 8.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 14.2 The application must be made by claim form under Part 8.] 14.3 Every person (other than the claimant) who appears in the register as mortgagor or mortgagee of the aircraft concerned must be made a defendant to the claim.

## 14.4 A copy of the claim form must be sent to the Civil Aviation Authority.

## 14.5 The application will be assigned to the Chancery Division.

## 14.6 The Civil Aviation Authority is entitled to be heard in the proceedings.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 14.6 The Civil Aviation Authority is entitled to be heard in the proceedings.] 15.1 This paragraph applies to an application under section 344 of the Insolvency Act 1986 to register an assignment of book debts.

## 15.2 The application must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.2 The application must be made—] (1) by claim form under Part 8; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.2 The application must be made—] (2) by witness statement.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.2 The application must be made—] 15.3 The application must be made to a Master of the King’s Bench Division and accompanied by payment of the prescribed fee.

## 15.4 Where the application is made by witness statement—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.4 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (1) Part 23 applies to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.4 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (2) the witness statement constitutes the application notice under that Part;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.4 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (3) the witness statement does not need to be served on any other person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.4 Where the application is made by witness statement—] (4) the application will normally be dealt with without a hearing.

## 15.5 The application—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.5 The application—] (1) must have exhibited to it a true copy of the assignment and of every schedule to it;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.5 The application—] (2) must set out the particulars of the assignment and the parties to it; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.5 The application—] (3) must verify the date and time of the execution of the assignment, and its execution in the presence of a witness.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 15.5 The application—] 15.6 Upon the court being satisfied, the documents so exhibited will be filed and the particulars of the assignment and of the parties to it entered in the register.

## Application under section 42 of the Senior Courts Act 1981

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Application under section 42 of the Senior Courts Act 1981] 16.1 An application under section 42 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 is heard and determined by a Divisional Court.

## 16.2 The claim form must be filed at the Administrative Court and—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 16.2 The claim form must be filed at the Administrative Court and—] (1) be accompanied by a witness statement in support; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 16.2 The claim form must be filed at the Administrative Court and—] (2) be served on the person against whom the order is sought.

## Application for detailed assessment of a returning officer’s account

## 17.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (1) An application by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (a) the Secretary of State under section 30 of the Representation of the People Act 1983 or paragraph 4 of Schedule 1 to the Recall of MPs Act 2015;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (b) the Welsh Ministers under article 24 of the National Assembly for Wales (Representation of the People) Order 2007; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (c) the Electoral Commission under paragraph 17 of Schedule 3 to the European Union Referendum Act 2015,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] for the detailed assessment of a returning officer’s account must be made by claim form.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (2) In this paragraph and paragraphs 17.3 to 17.5 and 17.8, references to the returning officer are to be read—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (a) for applications under the Recall of MPs Act 2015, as references to the petition officer;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (b) for applications under the National Assembly for Wales (Representation of the People) Order 2007, as references to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (i) the constituency returning officer, in relation to a constituency election; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (ii) the constituency and regional returning officer, in relation to a regional election; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] (c) for applications under the European Union Referendum Act 2015, as references to the counting officer or Regional Counting Officer.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] 17.2 When it issues the claim form, the court will fix a date for the hearing of the detailed assessment to be dealt with if the application is granted.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] 17.3 The returning officer may, on the application, apply to the court to examine any claim made against him in respect of matters charged in the account.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.1] 17.4 To make an application under paragraph 17.3, the returning officer must file an application within 7 days of being served with a copy of the application for detailed assessment.

## 17.5 When an application is filed under paragraph 17.3, the court will—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.5 When an application is filed under paragraph 17.3, the court will—] (a) fix a date for the hearing;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.5 When an application is filed under paragraph 17.3, the court will—] (b) give notice of the hearing date to the returning officer; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.5 When an application is filed under paragraph 17.3, the court will—] (c) serve a copy of the application and notice of hearing on the claimant.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.5 When an application is filed under paragraph 17.3, the court will—] 17.6 The examination and detailed assessment may take place on the same day, provided that the examination is determined before the detailed assessment is concluded.

## 17.7 The district judge may hear and determine—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.7 The district judge may hear and determine—] (a) an application for detailed assessment;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.7 The district judge may hear and determine—] (b) any application under paragraph 17.3.

## 17.8 The court will serve a copy of the order made in the application on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.8 The court will serve a copy of the order made in the application on—] (a) the Secretary of State;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.8 The court will serve a copy of the order made in the application on—] (b) the returning officer; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 17.8 The court will serve a copy of the order made in the application on—] (c) in an application under paragraph 17.3, the claimant.

## Other proceedings under the Representation of the People Acts

## 18.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 18.1] (1) This paragraph applies to proceedings under the Representation of the People Acts (other than proceedings under section 30 of the Representation of the People Act 1983) and the European Union Referendum (Conduct) Regulations 2016 (“the 2016 Regulations”).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 18.1] (2) The jurisdiction of the High Court under those Acts in matters relating to Parliamentary and local government elections, or under the 2016 Regulations, will be exercised by a Divisional Court except that—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 18.1] (a) any jurisdiction, under a provision of any of those Acts, or under the 2016 Regulations, exercisable by a single judge will be exercised by a single judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 18.1] (b) any jurisdiction, under any such provision, exercisable by a Master will be exercised by a Master; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 18.1] (c) where the court’s jurisdiction in matters relating to Parliamentary elections is exercisable by a single judge, that jurisdiction in matters relating to local government elections is also exercisable by a single judge.

## Application under Mental Health Act 1983

## 19.1 In this paragraph—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.1 In this paragraph—] (1) a section referred to by a number refers to the section so numbered in the Mental Health Act 1983 and ‘Part II’ means Part II of that Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.1 In this paragraph—] (2) ‘hospital manager’ means the manager of a hospital as defined in section 145(1) of the Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.1 In this paragraph—] (3) ‘place of residence’ means, in relation to a patient who is receiving treatment as an in-patient in a hospital or other institution, that hospital or institution.

## 19.2 The claim form must be filed—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (1) in the County Court hearing centre serving the patient’s place of residence is situated; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (2) in the case of an application under section 30, in the court or County Court hearing centre that made the order under section 29 which the application seeks to discharge or vary.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] 19.3 Where an application is made under section 29 for an order that the functions of the nearest relative of the patient are to be exercisable by some other person –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (1) the nearest relative must be made a respondent, unless—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (a) the application is made on the grounds that the patient has no nearest relative or that it is not reasonably practicable to ascertain whether he has a nearest relative; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (b) the court orders otherwise; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (2) the court may order that any other person shall be made a respondent.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] 19.4 Subject to paragraph 18.5, the court may accept as evidence of the facts relied upon in support of the application, any report made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (1) by a medical practitioner; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (2) by any of the following acting in the course of their official duties—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (a) a probation officer;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (b) an officer of a local authority;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (c) an officer of a voluntary body exercising statutory functions on behalf of a local authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] (d) an officer of a hospital manager.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.2 The claim form must be filed—] 19.5 The respondent must be informed of the substance of any part of the report dealing with his fitness or conduct that the court considers to be material to the determination of the claim.

## 19.6 An application under Part II shall be heard in private unless the court orders otherwise.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 19.6 An application under Part II shall be heard in private unless the court orders otherwise.] 19.7 The judge may, for the purpose of determining the application, interview the patient. The interview may take place in the presence of, or separately from, the parties. The interview may be conducted elsewhere than at the court. Alternatively, the judge may direct the district judge to interview the patient and report to the judge in writing.

## Applications under section 13 of the Coroners Act 1988

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 13 of the Coroners Act 1988] 20.1 An application under section 13 of the Coroners Act 1988 is heard and determined by a Divisional Court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > Applications under section 13 of the Coroners Act 1988] 20.2 The application must, unless made by the Attorney General, be accompanied by the Attorney General’s fiat.

## 20.3 The claim form must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 20.3 The claim form must—] (1) state the grounds for the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 20.3 The claim form must—] (2) be filed at the Administrative Court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 20.3 The claim form must—] (3) be served upon all persons directly affected by the application within six weeks of the grant of the Attorney General’s fiat.

## Application for injunction to prevent environmental harm or unlicensed activities

## 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] (1) section 187B or 214A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] (2) section 44A of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] (3) section 26AA of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] (4) section 12 or 26 of the Energy Act 2008.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] 21.2 An injunction may be granted under those sections against a person whose identity is unknown to the applicant.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.1 This paragraph relates to applications under—] 21.3 In this paragraph, an injunction refers to an injunction under one of those sections and ‘the defendant’ is the person against whom the injunction is sought.

## 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—] (1) a photograph;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—] (2) a thing belonging to or in the possession of the defendant; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—] (3) any other evidence.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—] 21.5 The description of the defendant under paragraph 20.4 must be sufficiently clear to enable the defendant to be served with the proceedings.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.4 In the claim form, the applicant must describe the defendant by reference to—] (The court has power under Part 6 to dispense with service or make an order permitting service by an alternative method or at an alternative place).

## 21.6 The application must be accompanied by a witness statement. The witness statement must state—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.6 The application must be accompanied by a witness statement. The witness statement must state—] (1) that the applicant was unable to ascertain the defendant’s identity within the time reasonably available to him;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.6 The application must be accompanied by a witness statement. The witness statement must state—] (2) the steps taken by him to ascertain the defendant’s identity;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.6 The application must be accompanied by a witness statement. The witness statement must state—] (3) the means by which the defendant has been described in the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 49E – ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR CLAIMS > 21.6 The application must be accompanied by a witness statement. The witness statement must state—] (4) that the description is the best the applicant is able to provide.
